heard: Astronomers first saw a faint violet speck, calling it an ordinary star. In 1957, Mexican astronomers catalogued it as entry 618, unaware of the monster lurking 10.8 billion light years away. This point of light is an ultramassive black hole with an event horizon radius of 1,300 astronomical units. That is 40 times Pluto's distance from the sun, all contained within one dark sphere. Gas whipping around the void at 10,000 kilometers per second fuels a brilliance equal to 140 trillion suns. Initial measurements found 66 billion solar masses, later revised to 40.7 billion suns. Wrapped in a glowing hydrogen nebula over 300,000 light years across, it remains one of the heaviest objects in existence. No monster in the cosmos has ever hidden behind such a quiet disguise.
